gloss: crawling on the ground; creeping along with one's body close to the surface

definitions.gloss: crawling on the ground; creeping along with one's body close to the surface
definitions.explanation: crawling on the ground; creeping along with one's body close to the surface

examples.japanese: {匍匐|ほふく}{前進|ぜんしん}する。
{兵士|へいし}たちは{低|ひく}い{姿勢|しせい}で{匍匐|ほふく}した。
examples.english: The soldiers crawled along in a low posture.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}に{見|み}つからないように、{地面|じめん}を{匍匐|ほふく}して{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: We crawled along the ground to avoid being spotted by the enemy.

notes:
Refers to moving forward on hands and knees or with the body flat against the ground. Most commonly encountered in military contexts, where {匍匐|ほふく}{前進|ぜんしん} (crawling advance) is a standard training exercise.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {匍匐|ほふく}{前進|ぜんしん} — crawling forward (military drill)
- {匍匐|ほふく}して{進|すす}む — to advance by crawling
- {地面|じめん}を{匍匐|ほふく}する — to crawl along the ground

USAGE:
Also used in botany to describe plants that spread by creeping along the ground ({匍匐|ほふく}{茎|けい} — creeping stem/stolon). In everyday Japanese, this is a literary or technical word; casual speech would use {這|は}う instead.
